review: 1:4 כְּרֵיחַ הַבֹּשֶׂם — 'like the scent of perfume'; the Arabic كَشَذَا طِيبٍ is a construct of scent and sweetness, and Hebrew keeps a single construct to fit four words.
3:4 שִׁלֵּם כָּל־חוֹבֵנוּ — 'He paid all our debt'; the Arabic كُلَّ دَيْنِنَا وَفَى is the same commercial image, and שִׁלֵּם is the biblical verb for making good a debt (Ps 76:12).
4:2 הוּא חֶלְקִי הַטּוֹב — the Arabic نِعْمَ النَّصِيب is the nعْمَ superlative ('the best portion'); Hebrew has no such construction at four syllables, so the adjective carries it.
5:4 אַחֲרֵי הַמּוֹפֵת — 'after the wonder/sign'; the Arabic الْمِثَال is 'example', and מוֹפֵת is chosen for the assonance with the previous line's שְׁלֵמוּת.
6:1–6:2 הַנִּבְזֶה … לַגְּמוּל — the Arabic مَنْ أُهِينَ ('the One despised') is Isa 53:3 (נִבְזֶה), and גְּמוּל is the biblical word for recompense (Isa 59:18).
